findings.title: osTicket v1.14.8/v1.15.4 Available
findings.summary_md: osTicket released v1.14.8 and v1.15.4 as security updates and strongly recommended applying the upgrade immediately. The vendor said the releases fixed multiple security vulnerabilities, with the fixes also integrated into v1.15.4 for installations on the older maintenance branch. The post identifies v1.14.8 as the maintenance option for users unable or unwilling to move to v1.15.4.

findings.title: Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in geoserver
findings.summary_md: The GeoServer advisory describes unauthenticated RCE on default installations through crafted OGC parameters that cause property names to be evaluated as XPath expressions. It says the flaw applies to all GeoServer instances and lists patched releases 2.22.6, 2.23.6, 2.24.4 and 2.25.2. The documented workaround removes `gt-complex-x.y.jar` or replaces the `gt-app-schema`, `gt-complex` and `gt-xsd-core` jars, with warnings that removal can break functionality.

findings.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2024-36401, the OSGeo GeoServer GeoTools evaluation-injection vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. The alert says Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by the catalog due date and urges all organizations to prioritize KEV remediation.

findings.title: CISA warns critical Geoserver GeoTools RCE flaw is exploited in attacks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported that Shadowserver first observed exploitation of CVE-2024-36401 on July 9, 2024, shortly after public proof-of-concept exploits appeared. It cited ZoomEye's estimate of approximately 16,462 internet-exposed GeoServer servers and noted patched versions 2.23.6, 2.24.4 and 2.25.2. The article urged exposed installations to patch immediately and review systems and logs for compromise.
